title: How Much Do Medical Interpreters Cost? A Healthcare Budget Guide
summary: Learn what medical interpreters really cost across in-house staffing, contracted services, and on-demand models.
body_markdown:
###


The answer depends on the staffing model. BLS reports a $63,000 median annual wage for interpreters and translators working in hospitals in May 2025. Contracted in-person interpretation can exceed $100 per hour for harder-to-source languages, while remote and AI services use different pricing structures. The better budgeting metric is total cost per completed interpreted encounter.


###


In-house staffing makes the most financial sense when one language has dense, predictable demand that keeps the interpreter busy with interpretation work. Compare annual outsourced spend for that language with the fully loaded cost of an interpreter FTE, then account for coverage, paid leave, and simultaneous demand.


###


At least 4.2 full-time equivalents are needed to cover 168 hours in a week at 40 hours per FTE, before accounting for vacation, sick leave, shift overlap, or multiple simultaneous encounters. Actual staffing requirements are higher when continuous coverage is required.


###


Hourly or salaried rates do not show how much paid time is spent interpreting. An interpreter who is paid for eight hours but actively interprets for four has a much higher effective cost per productive interpretation hour. Minimums, travel, connection time, and administrative overhead create the same effect for outsourced services.


###


Match the delivery model to demand. Staff high-volume languages internally when the workload supports it, use on-demand services for variable demand, and avoid paying for idle capacity across the long tail of languages. Measure cost per completed encounter instead of focusing only on rate cards.
